name: Prior Art and Clearance Searching
title: Prior Art and Clearance Searching
answer: Prior art and clearance searching is the practice of finding earlier patents, publications, trademarks, and other disclosures that affect whether an invention is patentable or a mark is registrable and usable. It covers patentability searches, freedom to operate searches, trademark clearance searches, and sometimes design and copyright checks. The work sits inside intellectual property and trademark strategy, where it informs filing decisions, product launches, and risk assessments. It is distinct from litigation searching, though the same databases and methods often overlap.

sections.body: Prior art and clearance searching is the practice of finding earlier patents, publications, trademarks, and other disclosures that affect whether an invention is patentable or a mark is registrable and usable. It covers patentability searches, freedom to operate searches, trademark clearance searches, and sometimes design and copyright checks. The work sits inside intellectual property and trademark strategy, where it informs filing decisions, product launches, and risk assessments. It is distinct from litigation searching, though the same databases and methods often overlap.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on patent and trademark office databases such as the USPTO, EPO, and WIPO, plus national registers and commercial platforms like Derwent, Orbit, and PatBase. AI tools increasingly add semantic search, clustering, and image similarity, and the site tracks 732 AI tools that may include such search assistants. The infrastructure also includes classification systems such as CPC, IPC, and the Nice classes, along with citation networks and legal status data. Access may be through APIs, bulk data, or subscription interfaces.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A searcher defines the invention or mark, then builds a search strategy with keywords, synonyms, classification codes, and assignee or applicant filters. They run iterative queries, review hits, and expand or narrow using citations, family members, and legal status. For trademarks, they check identical and similar marks in relevant classes and jurisdictions, and they assess likelihood of confusion. Results are compiled into a search report with relevance ratings and claim charts or mark comparisons.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Patent applicants and their attorneys owe a duty of candor and disclosure to patent offices, so prior art found in a search may need to be submitted. Missing relevant art can affect validity and, in some jurisdictions, expose a patent to inequitable conduct allegations. Trademark clearance carries risk of opposition or infringement claims, and the site tracks 150 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which shows how disputes can arise. Provenance matters: search reports record databases, dates, queries, and the searcher's identity, and confidentiality and privilege are maintained where applicable.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: AI-assisted search is becoming more common, with large language models and vector search helping to surface conceptually similar art and marks beyond exact keywords. Patent offices are adopting AI for classification and examination, and the site tracks 29 AI case law precedents that may shape how courts treat search and disclosure duties. More automated monitoring, continuous clearance, and integration with product lifecycle tools are likely. The open questions include how much human review is required and how to document AI-assisted findings for evidentiary purposes.
